framework.name: Swiss ISG (SR 128)
framework.description: Swiss Federal Act on Information Security (ISG / LSI, SR 128) — in force 1 January 2024, cyberattack reporting obligation in force 1 April 2025. Mandatory for federal bodies; applicable to critical infrastructure operators via Art. 74a-74h. ISO 27001 is the recognised implementation vehicle.

objects.title: Information Security Principles
objects.description: Core security obligations: CIA triad, organisational accountability, risk management, third-party requirements, and incident response (Art. 6–10a).

objects.title: Information Classification
objects.description: Classification scheme, authority, levels (internal / confidential / secret), and access controls for classified information (Art. 11–15).

objects.title: ICT Security
objects.description: IT security procedure, security categories (baseline / elevated / very high), minimum security measures, and operational security (Art. 16–19).

objects.title: Personnel & Access
objects.description: Access conditions for personnel including background screening, training, and restrictive need-to-know authorisation principles (Art. 20–21).

objects.title: Physical Security
objects.description: Physical protection of information assets and IT systems; establishment of security zones for classified areas (Art. 22–23).

objects.title: Personnel Security Checks
objects.description: Identification of sensitive functions, personnel security clearance procedures, and periodic repetition of checks (Art. 27–30, 43).

objects.title: Cyberattack Reporting Obligation
objects.description: Mandatory reporting of cyberattacks to BACS/OFCS within 24 hours — applies to critical infrastructure operators listed in Art. 74b (in force 1 April 2025).

objects.title: ISMS Organisation
objects.description: Appointment of information security officers and adoption of the Federal Council standard security requirements (Art. 81, 85).

objects.title: Information Security Policy — CIA Triad
objects.description: Authorities and organisations ensure information is confidential, available, integral, and traceable, proportionate to the risk to public interests (Art. 6 al. 2).

objects.title: Organisational Accountability
objects.description: Authorities organise, implement, and control information security according to the state of scientific and technical knowledge; set objectives and risk management principles (Art. 7).

objects.title: Information Security Risk Management
objects.description: Risks in the domain of information security are continuously evaluated; necessary measures are taken to eliminate or reduce risks to an acceptable level; residual risks are formally accepted (Art. 8).

objects.title: Third-Party Security Requirements
objects.description: When collaborating with third parties, ISG requirements and measures are included in contracts and agreements; implementation of measures is monitored (Art. 9).

objects.title: Security Incident Response
objects.description: Security breaches are detected rapidly, causes clarified, and consequences limited; action plans exist for serious incidents; exercises are conducted (Art. 10).

objects.title: Information Classification Principles
objects.description: Information meeting the criteria of Art. 13 is classified; classification is limited to what is strictly necessary and is temporary where possible (Art. 11).

objects.title: Classification Authority
objects.description: Competent persons and services are designated to classify information; classification accuracy is periodically verified (Art. 12).

objects.title: Classification Levels
objects.description: Three classification levels are applied: internal (nuisance risk), confidential (significant harm), secret (serious harm to public interests) (Art. 13).

objects.title: Access Control for Classified Information
objects.description: Access to classified information is restricted to authorised persons with a legitimate need-to-know or a formal access authorisation (Art. 14).

objects.title: ICT Security Procedure
objects.description: A documented ICT security procedure defines protection requirements assessment, security measure implementation and control, IT system authorisation, and incident response (Art. 16).

objects.title: ICT Security Categories
objects.description: IT systems are assigned to security categories: baseline protection (default), elevated protection, or very high protection based on potential harm to public interests (Art. 17).

objects.title: Minimum Security Measures
objects.description: Minimum security requirements are defined for each security category; all IT systems meet the baseline protection minimum; very-high protection systems undergo periodic effectiveness checks (Art. 18).

objects.title: Operational ICT Security
objects.description: The security of IT systems operated on behalf of the organisation or for a third party is guaranteed (Art. 19).

objects.title: Personnel Access Conditions
objects.description: Persons accessing information, IT systems, premises, and infrastructure are carefully selected, identified, trained, and where necessary committed to confidentiality (Art. 20).

objects.title: Restrictive Access Authorisation
objects.description: Access authorisations are granted only to persons who require them to perform their duties; authorisations are revoked at end of engagement or when security indicators arise (Art. 21).

objects.title: Physical Protection of Information Assets
objects.description: Adequate physical protection of information and IT systems against misuse and disruption is ensured (Art. 22).

objects.title: Security Zones
objects.description: Security zones are established where confidential/secret information is regularly processed or elevated/very-high IT systems are operated; appropriate physical controls are applied (Art. 23).

objects.title: Sensitive Function List
objects.description: A list of functions involving the exercise of a sensitive activity is established, maintained, and periodically verified within each area of competence (Art. 28).

objects.title: Personnel Security Clearances
objects.description: Persons exercising sensitive functions are subject to a security check (base or extended) before the activity is assigned; consent is obtained (Art. 29–32).

objects.title: Periodic Repetition of Security Checks
objects.description: Personnel security checks are repeated periodically: base checks every 5–10 years; extended checks every 3–5 years (Art. 43).

objects.title: Reporting Obligation Determination
objects.description: It is determined whether the organisation is subject to the mandatory cyberattack reporting obligation under Art. 74b (in force 1 April 2025); relevant persons are informed of the obligation (Art. 74a–74b).

objects.title: Cyberattack Classification Criteria
objects.description: Internal criteria exist to determine whether a cyberattack must be reported: jeopardises CI operations, involves data manipulation/exfiltration, was undetected for a prolonged period, or involves extortion (Art. 74d).

objects.title: 24-Hour Reporting to BACS/OFCS
objects.description: A procedure ensures cyberattacks are reported to BACS/OFCS within 24 hours of detection, including type, execution, effects, and measures taken; supplemented as new information becomes available (Art. 74e).

objects.title: Secure Reporting Channel
objects.description: The secure electronic reporting channel provided by BACS/OFCS is known and accessible; simultaneous reporting to other competent authorities is supported where required (Art. 74f).

objects.title: Monitoring for Reporting Compliance
objects.description: Internal processes ensure compliance with the reporting obligation; failure to report is treated as an infringement subject to administrative sanction up to CHF 100,000 (Art. 74g–74h).

objects.title: Information Security Officer
objects.description: An information security officer (ISB/RSSI) is formally appointed, with responsibility for advising, directing the ISMS organisation, and monitoring compliance; a deputy is designated (Art. 81).

objects.title: Standard Security Requirements
objects.description: The Federal Council standard security requirements (organisational, personnel, technical) are adopted as the baseline; authorities formally declare requirements mandatory where not already done (Art. 85).
